::: {.main-message}
Code is a written record of every decision you make with your data.
:::

## Run code


::: {.cell}
```{webr}
2 + 2
sqrt(144)
```
:::


- `sqrt()` is a **function**. Inputs go in brackets.

## Objects


::: {.cell}
```{webr}
n_crimes <- 1977
n_wards <- 3
n_crimes / n_wards
```
:::


- `<-` stores a result in an **object**.

## Data frames

- Read data straight from the web. Here: crimes recorded within a mile of Leeds Town Hall in August 2026, from the police.uk API (more on APIs in Part 1).


::: {.cell}
```{webr}
library(jsonlite)
library(dplyr)

crimes <- fromJSON("https://data.police.uk/api/crimes-street/all-crime?lat=53.7999&lng=-1.5492&date=2026-08") |>
  flatten()

nrow(crimes)
head(crimes$category)
table(crimes$category)
```
:::


- Rows = crimes. Columns = variables.
- `$` picks one column.

## The pipe `|>` ("and then")


::: {.cell}
```{webr}
crimes |>
  filter(category == "robbery") |>
  count(location.street.name, sort = TRUE)
```
:::


- `filter()` keeps rows. `count()` tallies them.
- "On or near Nightclub" is not a street. Hold that thought until Part 1.
- `==` compares. A single `=` doesn't.
- You will also see `%>%` in older code, books and the module. Same idea. `%>%` comes from the `magrittr` package (loaded with `dplyr`). `|>` has been built into R since version 4.1 (2021), so it needs no package. We use `|>`.

## Your turn

Which streets recorded the most **violent crime**?


::: {.cell setup='true' exercise='warmup_1'}
```{webr}
#| setup: true
#| exercise: warmup_1
library(dplyr); library(jsonlite)
crimes <- flatten(fromJSON("https://data.police.uk/api/crimes-street/all-crime?lat=53.7999&lng=-1.5492&date=2026-08"))
crimes$street_name <- crimes$location.street.name
```
:::



::: {.cell exercise='warmup_1'}
```{webr}
#| exercise: warmup_1
crimes |>
  filter(category == "______") |>
  count(______, sort = TRUE)
```
:::


::: {.hint exercise="warmup_1"}
The category is `"violent-crime"` (lower case, with a hyphen). Count by `street_name`.
:::

::: {.solution exercise="warmup_1"}
```r
crimes |>
  filter(category == "violent-crime") |>
  count(street_name, sort = TRUE)
```
:::

## Errors are normal


::: {.cell}
```{webr}
crimes |> filter(category == "Burglary") |> nrow()
Crimes |> nrow()
```
:::


- Line 1: 0 rows. R is case sensitive: the category is `burglary`.
- Line 2: error. There's no `Crimes`, only `crimes`.
- Read the error. Search it online.
